Ojo de Agua on Ometepe is a place to stop beside cool freshwater amid tropical greenery. The pools are fed by a natural underground spring, while tall trees shade the banks. It is a pleasant chance to take a break from the road and ferry crossing and relax by the water.

Clear water, green reflections, and the stone edges of the pools make Ojo de Agua one of the island's memorable natural spots. It can be included in a day trip around Ometepe or visited during a longer journey. Swimming conditions, the length of the stop, and the services included depend on the chosen itinerary.

Near the Zócalo, on Moneda Street, stands the former residence of Mexico City's archbishops. Its red facade and carved portal details draw attention to the architecture of the colonial center, where church and government buildings stand very close to one another.

Today, the old palace is also known as an art museum of Mexico's Ministry of Finance. It makes a peaceful stop on a walk through the capital, offering a chance to examine the building and recall the early history of the local Church, associated with Juan de Zumárraga. The organizer confirms which galleries are accessible on a particular excursion.

## Holguín — a city of parks in Cuba!

Holguín is a city in the province of the same name. It is often called the city of parks because it has many squares and houses nestled in the shade of trees. The city has relatively few buildings known for their colonial architecture.

Numerous monuments to heroes of battles fought during the wars of independence are scattered across the city. Bahía de Naranjo ("Orange Bay") Park lies 4 km from the city.

## Holguín — beach holidays in Cuba!

At the Coppo de Maita Museum, visitors can see excavations of an Indigenous settlement. Holguín is home to 30% of Cuba's endemic plant species, as well as more than 1,000 animal species, particularly birds and butterflies. The city has many beaches with beautiful sand and warm ocean water.
